obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System
basis: Applies to owners and operators of U.S.-flagged vessels, facilities and OCS facilities required to have a security plan under 33 CFR parts 104 to 106 (101.605(a)). The owner works onshore at customers' production facilities and owns no vessel, waterfront facility or OCS facility

citation: TSA SD Pipeline-2021-02G, issued under 49 U.S.C. 114
basis: Applies to owners and operators of TSA-notified critical pipelines or LNG facilities. The owner operates no pipeline and holds no TSA notice; no customer MSA passes pipeline requirements down. The incident reporting directive (SD Pipeline-2021-01G) reaches the same notified owners and operators only
Not a final rule; tracked. As proposed, the size test is the SBA standard for NAICS 213112 ($47.0 million, 13 CFR 121.201) against about $180,000 in receipts, and no proposed sector criterion is met

obligation: NIST CSF 2.0 with NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (voluntary benchmark)
basis: No binding federal sector cybersecurity rule reaches the business. Customer A's annual questionnaire is organized by CSF 2.0, and the laptop connects to customers' OT, so SP 800-82 Rev. 3 is applied to the owner's touch points

obligation: Customer A MSA security schedule, items (1) to (8)
citation: Customer A MSA (2025 renewal), security schedule
basis: Customer A (about 45% of receipts) requires 8 security items, including 24-hour incident notice, email approval of logic and setpoint changes, consent before sharing data with software services, and cyber coverage of at least $1 million while the owner holds remote access

obligation: Customers B, C and D MSA confidentiality clauses
citation: Customer B, C and D MSAs
basis: Standard confidentiality clauses only (information is confidential and returned on request); covered through the CSF rows and POL-01, not decomposed into rows

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (data security, breach notice, disposal)
basis: A covered entity includes a sole proprietorship that maintains personal information (501.171(1)(b)). The business holds names and Social Security numbers of 2 helpers (W-9 scans and 1099 records). The 500-person and 1,000-person notice duties cannot be reached at that volume; the disposal duty covers customer records, which the business does not hold, so POL-01 applies it voluntarily
Both helpers' W-9 forms show Florida addresses

obligation: PHMSA pipeline safety, including operator qualification
basis: Part 195 does not apply to onshore production facilities, including flow lines (195.1(b)(8)); operator qualification covers covered tasks on a pipeline facility under the operator's program. The MSAs cover production facilities and flow lines only

obligation: Oil discharge notice to the National Response Center
applies: Conditional (only if a release reaches water)
basis: The customer, as facility operator, is normally the person in charge; the owner tells the customer at once and calls only if acting as the person in charge on site with no customer contact reachable

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
basis: Applies to any U.S. person considering a ransom payment

obligation: Federal contract reporting of covered telecommunications and Kaspersky articles
basis: The business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts; its only customers are 4 private producers
No customer agreement designates or shares Sensitive Security Information; the work is on onshore production facilities
The owner works only with commercial field equipment and its configuration software; no export-controlled technology is held

obligation: Payment card industry data security standard (contract)
basis: The business accepts no payment cards; customers pay by ACH
